meta.descripcion: Personal page. A small number of the figures have been rounded generously.
cabecera.rol: Senior engineer · Ships before the requirement exists · No rollbacks to date
cabecera.resumen: Learns a new stack over a weekend and is reviewing other people’s code in it by Tuesday. Asks the question the room was about to ask, one day earlier. Works best alongside other people, whose throughput measurably improves and does not return to baseline afterwards.
logros.ayuda: Drag the card file to spin it, or use the arrow keys. It has inertia, friction and detents, like the one on the desk.
logros.01: Shipped the feature three quarters before Product wrote the requirement. By then it had been in the beta for two sprints, had 40,000 daily users, and the ticket was closed as already done.
logros.02: Optimized the network while writing the iptables rules. Throughput was up 40% before the firewall finished coming online, and the configuration was adopted as the reference across four regions.
logros.03: Refactored the authentication layer during the stand-up. The stand-up ran eleven minutes.
logros.04: Identified the root cause from the stack trace while the logs were still uploading, patched it on the call, and the incident was downgraded before the status page finished publishing.
logros.05: Migrated 1,200 services across two clouds with zero downtime. Monitoring recorded no event at all. Finance noticed first, when the invoice arrived 60% lower.
logros.06: Reviewed a 4,000-line pull request in one sitting and found the single race condition, which had not fired once in three years of production.
logros.07: Cut the build from 40 minutes to 9 seconds, then rewrote the cache layer so the second build took no time at all.
logros.08: Reduced p99 latency by 94% by deleting code. Net change: −3,100 lines.
logros.09: Wrote the documentation first. The implementation matched it exactly. Four years and nine releases later it still matches, diagrams included.
logros.10: Found a bug in the compiler. Upstream merged the patch in 48 hours.
logros.11: Learned the language on a Monday to unblock the team and shipped the library on Wednesday. By the next quarter it was a dependency of the framework that had blocked us.
logros.12: Paired with a junior for one afternoon. They now run the platform team, and two of the people they hired run their own.
nums.04.pie: services migrated with no recorded event
juego.ayuda: Janitor Joe (1984), by Kevin Bales. CGA platforms: climb the ladders sweeping up every scrap and do not touch the robots. Arrows to move and climb, space to jump; on a phone, the pad. Tap the screen to start.
sh.ayuda: A real shell over a pretend filesystem. It lives in the tab: no server, nothing stored, and a reload puts it back as it was. sha256 is the browser’s own and fnv is written by hand.
sh.bienvenida: Type help for the commands. Try cat logros.txt or sha256 README.
sh.help: files ls [-l -a] · cd · pwd · tree · cat · wc [-l] create mkdir [-p] · touch · echo text > file (>> appends) move cp [-r] · mv · rm [-r] hash sha256 file · fnv file other whoami · date · history · clear · help Tab completes, ↑ ↓ walk the history, Ctrl-L clears.

lab.help: 59 sorting algorithms written in Java, running in your browser as JavaScript and as WebAssembly. Watch them work, race them, and see how the O of a function is worked out. Open the lab
pie.nota: A small number of the figures above have been rounded generously. Two things have not: I like learning new things and I like working with people. The rest is open to discussion, ideally in person.
